'''Dan Abramovich''' ({{Langx|he|'דן אברמוביץ}}; born March 12, 1963) is an Israeli-American mathematician working in the fields of [[algebraic geometry]] and [[arithmetic geometry]].  As of 2019, he holds the title of L. Herbert Ballou University Professor at [[Brown University]], and he is an Elected Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |title=Fellows |publisher=ams.org |accessdate=April 25, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.math.brown.edu/~abrmovic/ |title=Dan Abramovich |publisher=brown.edu |accessdate=April 25, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.brown.edu/academics/math/faculty|publisher=Brown University|accessdate=12 July 2019|title=Faculty, Department of Mathematics}}</ref>

==Education ==
Abramovich received a bachelor's degree at [[Tel Aviv University]] in 1987 and completed a doctorate at [[Harvard University]] in 1991 under [[Joe Harris (mathematician)|Joe Harris]] (''Subvarieties of abelian varieties and of Jacobians of curves'').<ref>{{MathGenealogyProject|id=6808}}</ref>  From 1991 to 1994 he was [[C. L. E. Moore instructor]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. Thereafter he held faculty positions at [[Boston University]] from 1994 to 1999 and since 2003 has been Professor at [[Brown University]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dan Abramovich - Brown math department|url=https://www.math.brown.edu/~abrmovic/cv.pdf|website=Brown University|accessdate=October 23, 2017}}</ref> 

== Career ==
Among other topics, he has dealt with [[birational geometry]], the [[resolution of singularities]], [[Variety (universal algebra)|subvarieties]] of [[abelian varieties]], limits for the [[Torsion (algebra)|torsion]] of [[elliptic curves]], [[rational numbers|rational]] and [[integer]] points on [[algebraic varieties]] and [[moduli spaces]] of [[vector bundles]] on [[algebraic curves|curves]]. Together with [[José Felipe Voloch|Felipe Voloch]], in 1992 he succeeded in making progress toward proving the Mordell-Lang Conjecture in characteristic ''p'' (the full proof came later from [[Ehud Hrushovski]]). He has been a guest scholar at, among other institutions, the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], the [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]] in Bonn, the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] (MSRI), the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in Paris and at [[Institut des hautes études scientifiques|IHES]]. He was an invited speaker at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] ("Resolution of singularities of complex algebraic varieties and their families").<ref>[https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.09976 Arxiv]</ref> From 1996 to 1998 he was a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Fellow]]. He is a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].
